sections.title: Enactment 3
paragraphs: These Zoning Regulations for the Town of Montgomery are enacted in accordance with 5 the provisions 24 V.S.A. Chapter 117, the Vermont Municipal and Regional Planning 6 and Development Act, ("The Act" herein). 7

sections.title: Purpose 9
paragraphs: It is the purpose of the Montgomery Zoning Regulations to provide for orderly 11 community growth, to further the purposes established in S4302 of the Act, and to 12 implement the Town Plan. 13

Chapter 117, S4303(10) of the Act, 17 including the division of a parcel into two or more parcels; new construction, 18 reconstruction, conversion, structural alteration, relocation, or enlargement of any 19 building or other structure (see Section 4.1(A)(1)(a)), or of any mining, earth resource 20 extraction, and change in the use of any building or other structure, or land or extension 21 of use of land shall commence except in compliance with these Regulations. 22

sections.title: Severability 24
paragraphs: If any portion of the Zoning Regulations are held unconstitutional or invalid by a court of 26 competent jurisdiction, the unaffected portions shall remain in force, and for this 27 purpose the provisions of the Regulations are severable. 28

sections.title: Interpretation 30
paragraphs: The Zoning Regulations shall not repeal, abrogate or impair any other applicable land 32 use controls (including statutes, regulations, rules, ordinances, permits, easements, 33 deed restrictions, covenants or similar devices). However, in their interpretation and 34 application, the provisions of the Regulations shall be held to be minimum requirements 35 which shall take precedence over any concurrent and less restrictive control. It is also 36 hereby stated that in any conflict or dispute involving these Regulations, that the intent 37 shall be considered in resolving any ambiguity. 38

The Rural 1 Residential District provides for rural 2 residential and business land uses at 3 lower densities than the village centers 4 to preserve the traditional working 5 landscape and to maintain 6 Montgomery's rural character. Home-based 12 occupations and industries are 13 common throughout the Rural 14 Residential District. The Rural 15 Residential District encompasses the 16 areas outside of the village centers 17 along Class 3 town roads and state 18 highways (excluding those portions of 19 Rt. 58 east of Amadon Road), and 20 including those lands comprising 21 smaller forest blocks in town where 22 natural resource concerns are not a 23 primary concern (as in the 24 Conservation I & II Districts described 25 below). 26 3) Conservation I District. The purpose of the Conservation I District is to preserve 28 the ecological, cultural and economic value and function of forest blocks and the 29 natural resources they encompass as detailed in the current Montgomery Town 30 Plan. These include: To maintain healthy, viable populations of native wildlife; To 31 support active forest management as a means of supporting the local wood 32 products industry; To enhance outdoor recreation valued by residents and 33 visitors alike; To provide for the protection of source waters which feed rivers and 34 streams, including important aquatic habitats; And to maintain the aesthetics 35 associated with the agricultural and forested landscape. Those lands in 36 Conservation l are as shown on the official town zoning map. 37 4) Conservation II District. The Conservation II District consists of forest blocks at 39 1,600 feet in elevation and above. Placing restrictions on development is 40 essential due to the sensitive resources located there, including wildlife habitat, 41 steep slopes, shallow soils, headwaters, and the potential for development to 42 affect erosion or flood hazards downstream. Protection of these areas also 43 serves the ecological, cultural and economic benefits associated with the rural 44 character as described above. Those lands in Conservation II are as shown on 45 the official town zoning map. 46 Montgomery Zoning Regulations 2018 5) Hazard Area Overlay District. The purpose of this overlay district is to prevent 2 increases in flooding caused by development in flood hazard areas, to minimize 3 future public and private losses due to flood, and to promote the public health, 4 safety, and general welfare. Designation of this area is also required for 5 continued participation in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and is 6 regulated under Article 8 of these Regulations. Included are all areas in 7 Montgomery identified as areas of Special Flood Hazard on the National Flood 8 Insurance maps located at the Town Office building. 9 6) River Corridor Area Overlay. The River Corridor consists of a floodplain 11 corridor, including the stream and land adjacent to the stream, the dimensions of 12 which are determined using physical relations between the channel width and the 13 meander belt width. It identifies an area where stream processes may occur that 14 enable the stream to re-establish and maintain a stable slope and dimensions 15 over time. A stable stream slope occurs when a channel reaches a certain 16 length. This length is accommodated by a corridor of floodplain area described 17 as the meander belt. The River Corridor is a calculated belt width-based corridor 18 where erosion is minimized when stream equilibrium conditions are achieved. 19 River Corridor area boundaries attempt to capture lands most vulnerable to 20 fluvial erosion in the near term and indicate the type, magnitude, and frequency 21 of fluvial adjustments anticipated during flood events. The area can be mapped, 22 and is based on quality-assured fluvial geomorphic data (i.e., data that describe 23 the physical form and process of a riverine system). The River Corridor is 24 determined on the most current River Corridor Protection Area Map published by 25 the Vermont Agency of Natural Resources (ANR) which are hereby adopted by 26 reference and declared to be part of these regulations. A modification of the 27 River Corridor Map may be made upon application of the Selectboard to the 28 Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) pursuant to the DEC 29 publication Flood Hazard Area And River Corridor Protection Procedure, Section 30 5(c)(2). Application may be made to account for geomorphic and other physical 31 characteristics found in the field but not accounted for in the River Corridor Map. 32

subsections.label: B
subsections.title: Purpose. Conditional use approval requires compliance with standards addressing 27

Standards and 29 conditions emphasize considerations to identify, avoid, and/or mitigate off-site 30 impacts of a proposed project. Conditional use approval also considers a building's 31 and site design's consistency with the purpose and character of the district within 32 which it is located. Standards and conditions emphasize those considerations 33 related to internal layout of the site, its physical design and appearance as viewed 34 from off-site, and the functional integration of the site with surrounding properties 35 and uses. 36

subsections.label: E
subsections.title: Review Standards. The DRB may grant conditional use approval only upon finding 1
paragraphs: that the proposed development shall not result in an undue adverse effect on any of 2 the following: 3 1) The capacity of existing or planned community facilities. The DRB shall 5 consider the demand for community services and facilities resulting from the 6 proposed development, and determine whether that demand will exceed the 7 existing or planned capacity of existing facilities or services. In making such a 8 determination, the DRB will consider any capital program or budget in effect at 9 the time of application. 10 2) The character of the neighborhood area or district affected. The DRB shall 12 consider the location, scale, type, density, and intensity of the proposed 13 development in relation to the character of area likely to be affected by the 14 proposed development, as defined by the purpose(s) of the zoning district(s) 15 within which the project is located and specifically stated polices and standards 16 of the Montgomery Town Plan. 17 3) Traffic on roads and highways in the vicinity. The DRB shall consider the 19 projected impact of traffic resulting from the proposed development on the 20 capacity, safety, efficiency and use of affected roads, bridges, and intersections. 21 A traffic impact study may be required. 22 4) Maximum safety of vehicular and pedestrian circulation between the site 24 and the street network. Particular attention shall be given to visibility at 25 intersections, to traffic flow and control, to pedestrian safety and convenience, 26 and to access in case of emergency. 27 5) Adequacy of circulation, parking, and loading facilities. Particular 29 consideration shall be given to the effect of noise, glare or odors on adjoining 30 properties and state and town highways. Adequacy of provisions for erosion 31 control, runoff, refuse removal, service areas, and snow removal shall be 32 considered. 33 6) Conformance with applicable General Regulations and Specific Standards 35 in Article 6 and 7. 36 7) Other Town bylaws in effect. No development shall be approved in vio lation of 38 existing municipal bylaws and ordinances. 39 8) The utilization of renewable energy resources. The DRB shall consider 41 whether the proposed development will interfere with the sustainable use of 42 renewable energy resources, including the existing and future availability of and 43 access to such resources on adjoining properties. 44 Montgomery Zoning Regulations 2018

subsections.label: F
subsections.title: Conditions. The DRB shall have the power to impose reasonable conditions and 1
paragraphs: safeguards to avoid an undue adverse effect on the standards above, including but 2 not limited to, the following conditions: 3 1) The DRB may require project phasing or improvements necessary to 4 accommodate the proposed development to ensure that the demand for facilities 5 or services does not exceed existing or planned capacity. 6 2) The DRB may limit the scale or dimensions of the proposal. 7 3) The DRB may increase setback distances for non-residential uses which are 8 contiguous to residential uses, recreation uses, or natural areas. 9 4) The DRB may limit the hours of operation. 10 5) The DRB may limit outdoor storage of materials, goods, and equipment. 11 6) The DRB may require that outdoor storage of or work associated with goods, 12 parts, supplies, vehicles or machinery is inside a building or behind screening. 13 7) The DRB may attach conditions with regard to size and location of parking areas, 14 landscaping, and signs. 15 8) The DRB may require roadway improvements on-site or off-site, if deemed 16 necessary, to accommodate the increased traffic associated with the 17 development. Improvements may also include traffic calming, sidewalks, 18 crosswalks and other similar improvements. 19

subsections.label: G
subsections.title: Conservation Districts Standards. In addition to the review standards set forth in 21
paragraphs: subsection F above, the DRB will also determine that proposed development in the 22 Conservation I & II Districts comply with the following standards when granting 23 conditional use approval. 24 1) Development will be designed and located to minimize encroachment (e.g., the 25 placement of buildings and the extension of roads, driveways and utilities) into presently 26 undeveloped, forested areas. All feasible building sites should be considered and the 27 development located as close to existing roads, other development and disturbed areas 28 as practical in order to maintain large areas of contiguous, undeveloped forest land. 29 2) Development will not result in an undue, adverse impact on significant wildlife 30 habitat as identified in the current Town Plan. The DRB will consider available 31 information and inventories of wildlife habitat, and should reference natural resource 32 inventories developed by the Conservation Commission and adopted by the Select 33 board, and may consult Vermont Department of Fish & Wildlife or other experts to 34 determine the presence of various habitats and to ensure that development is designed 35 to minimize undue adverse impacts (e.g., impacts that would significantly reduce the 36 ability of the particular habitat to continue supporting particular wildlife species that rely 37 on that habitat for specific functions). 38 3) Development will be located to avoid slopes exceeding fifteen (15) percent 39 gradient unless such development is necessary to achieve the most desirable design for 40 a site (e.g., if it would avoid impacts to other identified resources). In the event 41 development on steep slopes is allowed, clearing, excavation and filling on such lands 42 will be limited to the greatest extent practical and the preparation and implementation of 43 an erosion control plan may be required in accordance with Section 6.12. In no instance 44 will development be allowed on slopes greater than twenty-five (25) percent. 45 Montgomery Zoning Regulations 2018 4) The division of land will be configured to minimize the fragmentation of large tracts 1 of forest land, being as identified in the current Town Plan, and described in the most 2 current natural resource inventory developed by the Conservation Commission and 3 adopted by the Selectboard.
